headline: Growth continues, margins narrow, guidance raised
summary_short: Leidos grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 7.2% y/y to $4,558M (4% organic) but net income attributable to Leidos fell 9.5% y/y to $354M ($2.81 diluted EPS) on acquisition and restructuring costs; non-GAAP diluted EPS still rose 1.6% y/y to $3.26 and the company raised its full-year 2026 guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.2% y/y (4% organic) on Homeland (+32%, aided by the ENTRUST acquisition and Air Traffic/Energy demand) and Intelligence & Digital (+6%) growth, while Health fell 8% on lower medical disability exam volumes. Consolidated operating margin fell to 11.3% from 13.4% on $29M of Entrust/Analogic-JV/NorthStar-2030 costs and a year-ago $25M insurance gain that didn't repeat; net income fell 9.5% y/y to $354M ($2.81 diluted EPS), though non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 1.6% to $3.26. Net bookings of $4.9B (book-to-bill 1.1) lifted backlog to $48.7B. Cash was $748M after $300M debt paydown and $127M returned to shareholders. Leidos raised FY2026 revenue, EPS, and cash-flow guidance.

drivers.explanation: Homeland grew 32% (incl. $141M from the ENTRUST acquisition) on Air Traffic and Energy demand; Intelligence & Digital grew 6% on contract awards and IC mission-support volumes; Health fell 8% on lower medical disability exam volumes.
Operating cash flow rose to $793M from $486M, aided by a $90M swing in income taxes receivable/payable and higher accrued payroll; capex was roughly flat ($32M vs $29M).
Margin fell to 13.8% from 15.2% because the year-ago quarter included one-time, non-operational gains, including a $25M insurance reimbursement for legal costs, that didn't repeat.
Tracks GAAP EPS after adding back $29M of acquisition/restructuring costs and $40M of intangible amortization; benefit per share was aided by ~3% fewer diluted shares y/y (126M vs 130M).

Reflects $29M of costs tied to the ENTRUST acquisition, the pending Analogic joint venture, and NorthStar 2030 restructuring, plus the absence of the year-ago one-time gains noted for Adjusted EBITDA.
Tracks the net-income decline; partly offset by 3% fewer diluted shares outstanding (126M vs 130M) from continued buybacks.
Rose in line with revenue growth; also includes asset markdowns from restructuring activities booked to cost of revenues this quarter.
Revenue growth (+7.2%) outpaced the rise in cost of revenues (+7.8%); not separately explained beyond segment-level commentary.

Health margin narrowed to 23.4% from 25.8% on lower disability-exam volumes, and Corporate costs rose to $58M from $9M on higher unallocated restructuring/M&A costs, only partly offset by margin gains in Homeland and Defense.
Tracks the operating-income decline; interest expense also rose to $69M from $55M on higher debt following the Entrust acquisition financing.
Reflects the operating-income decline plus higher net interest expense ($69M vs $55M) following debt issued to fund the Entrust acquisition.
Cash funded the $2.3B Entrust acquisition and $300M of commercial-paper repayment in the first half, partly offset by debt issuance and $1.09B of year-to-date operating cash flow.

CEO Tom Bell called it 'another strong quarter,' citing $5B in contract awards and growth across Defense Tech, Energy Infrastructure, and Cyber; the company raised FY2026 guidance for revenue, EPS, and operating cash flow.
